catalog_quote: L’accent en bribri tombe invariablement sur la dernière syllabe du morphème. Il se matérialise par une intensité plus importante et par un noyau vocalique moins bref que ne le sont les noyaux non accentués. ... Le système tonal du bribri oppose deux tons : haut vs descendant. L’opposition n’est attestée que dans les syllabes accentuées. Les syllabes non accentuées sont produites avec un ton bas par défaut. ... Les mots bribri étant souvent constitués de plusieurs morphèmes, plusieurs syllabes « accentuées » (syllabes finales de morphèmes) peuvent cohabiter au sein de cette unité. Dans ce cas de figure, souvent, une seule d’entre elles conserve son intensité et son ton distinctif. Les autres se réalisent généralement avec une intensité égale à celles des syllabes non accentuées, et le ton est neutralisé à moyen ou bas. sweep_summary: Bribri (brib1243) is in the catalog as 'morphological' (accent invariably on the morpheme-final syllable; two tones H vs falling contrast only in accented syllables) on Chevrier 2017. this search of works with stress in the title turned up a single title: Constenla Umaña 1985, 'Prosodic Nasality in Bribri (Chibchan) and Universals of Nasality', IJAL 51(4): 374-376 (DOI 10.1086/465898). It is a 2-page note on regressive nasal spreading, not on accent placement; every open route was tried (UChicago 403, JSTOR JS wall, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar closed with no repository copy, archive.org 0 hits, no archived copy at the Internet Archive), so it stays paywalled and unread; its bibliographic records are and. Chevrier 2017 (held) summarizes it: domain of nasal spread = word; it uses 'toniques' vs 'atones' syllables with the morpheme-final syllable the tonic one, and the p.375 forms Chevrier reproduces carry final stress — all consistent with the catalog's classification, so priority for acquisition is low. Verification done in this search of works with stress in the title: the catalog's deciding quotation is verbatim at line 5122 (sec. 2.6.1, p.93) of the Chevrier text we hold ('L'accent en bribri tombe invariablement sur la dernière syllabe du morphème..'), and the held Jara Murillo 2018 grammar sec. 2.3 p.22 independently states the same picture ('Wilson (1982: xix) caracteriza el bribri como una lengua de acento tonal.. "[e]n cada palabra no compuesta hay generalmente, sino siempre, un solo tono que funciona como acento en palabras de más de una sílaba".. las sílabas con vocal de tono bajo son inacentuadas' and 'La oposición tonal suele aparecer en sílaba final de morfema'). Both are already in the record, so no new first-hand stress statement was read and nothing supersedes Chevrier 2017. only direct downloads and API lookups were possible.

new_statements.quote: Bribri has been described as having four lexical tones, two level tones, high and low, one fall (Lehmann 1920; Wilson 1974; Constenla 1981; Constenla, Elizondo & Pereira 1998, henceforth CEP98), and a glottal stop that is undergoing tonogenesis (Wilson 1996, CEP98, Jara 2004). [...] The tones are divided into two registers, [+high] for high and falling, and [-high] for low and rising. This classification has consequences for the syllables that have been supposed to be "neutral": Neutral syllables followed by a [+high] register tone are [3], but those followed by [-high] are phonetically one [1], suggesting a register spread from the final toned syllable to those preceding it.

tone_statements.citation: Krohn, Haakon S. 2022. Análisis acústico de las cualidades vocálicas en la lengua bribri. Lingüística y Literatura (Universidad de Antioquia) no. 81.
tone_statements.quote: Por añadidura, cada vocal aparece con tono alto/ascendente en una palabra y tono descendente en otra, por si el tono influyera en la cualidad vocálica. De esta manera, se pretendió evitar, en el mayor grado posible, la influencia de sonidos contiguos o factores suprasegmentales5. ... 5. Con respecto a los tonos, se obvió el contraste entre tonos alto y ascendente postulado en varias ocasiones (Constenla, Elizondo & Pereira, 1998) para el dialecto de Amubre, ya que no es nada evidente que se trate de un contraste fonológico.
tone_statements.translation: In addition, each vowel appears with high/rising tone in one word and falling tone in another, in case tone should influence vowel quality. In this way the aim was to avoid, as far as possible, the influence of neighbouring sounds or suprasegmental factors. ... n. 5: As regards the tones, the contrast between high and rising tones postulated on several occasions (Constenla, Elizondo & Pereira 1998) for the Amubre dialect was set aside, since it is not at all evident that it is a phonological contrast.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 5.1 'Análisis de lectura cuidadosa' and footnote 5, p. 38
tone_statements.summary: Acoustic vowel study; tone only as elicitation control (high/rising vs falling words); author doubts a phonemic high vs rising contrast (Amubre). No inventory or count. Annex 1: 24 tone-marked words.

tone_statements.citation: Coto-Solano, Rolando. 2021. Explicit Tone Transcription Improves ASR Performance in Extremely Low-Resource Languages: A Case Study in Bribri. In Proceedings of the First Workshop on Natural Language Processing for Indigenous Languages of the Americas (AmericasNLP 2021), 173-184. Association for Computational Linguistics.
tone_statements.quote: Bribri has four tones: high, falling, rising, and low tone. The first three are marked in the orthography using diacritics (respectively: à, á, â), while the low tone is left unmarked: a. Bribri tone can create differences in meaning: the word alà means ‘child’; its first syllable is low and the second syllable is high. Contrast this with alá ‘thunder’, where the second syllable has a falling tone.
tone_statements.summary: Four lexical tones on the (orthographic) vowel: high (grave), falling (acute), rising (circumflex), low (unmarked, most frequent); nasality a separate suprasegmental; no statement about stress/accent.

tone_statements.quote: Las sílabas tónicas son las únicas que presentan un tonema fonológicamente contrastivo, lo cual quiere decir que el bribri puede denominarse una lengua de acento tonal contrastivo, como indicado por Wilson (1982, p. xxiii). Los tonos contrastivos son, por lo menos, dos: alto/ascendente y descendente. ... En términos de la fonología autosegmental, las sílabas de tono alto están asociadas con el elemento tonal H (alto), mientras que las de tono descendente se vinculan con una secuencia de dos tonos, H y L (alto y bajo). En contraste, todas las sílabas inacentuadas se pronuncian con tono bajo, o neutro, el cual debe considerarse el tono por defecto.
tone_statements.translation: Tonic syllables are the only ones that show a phonologically contrastive toneme, which means Bribri can be called a language with contrastive tonal accent, as indicated by Wilson (1982: xxiii). The contrastive tones are at least two: high/rising and falling. ... In autosegmental terms, high-tone syllables are associated with the tonal element H, while falling-tone syllables are linked to a sequence of two tones, H and L. By contrast, all unaccented syllables are pronounced with low, or neutral, tone, which must be considered the default tone.

tone_statements.quote: En el habla bribri en que se basa este análisis (la de Soqui, lugar a orillas del río Urén en las cercanías de Amubre, Talamanca) los niveles tonales son dos: alto ... y bajo ... Estos niveles pueden darse solos o en dos combinaciones sobre una misma vocal: alto-bajo ... y bajo-alto ... En el habla estudiada se nota una clara oposición entre dos tipos de sílabas que se denominan aquí sílabas fuertes y sílabas débiles. Las primeras son más intensas y largas que las segundas ... Las oposiciones tonales se neutralizan en las sílabas débiles. ... Las sílabas finales de los morfemas polisilábicos bribris son siempre sílabas fuertes, al igual que las que integran los morfemas monosilábicos
tone_statements.translation: In the Bribri speech on which this analysis is based (that of Soqui, on the Uren river near Amubre, Talamanca) there are two tone levels: high and low. These levels can occur alone or in two combinations on a single vowel: high-low and low-high. ... In the speech studied there is a clear opposition between two types of syllables, here called strong and weak syllables. The former are more intense and longer than the latter ... The tonal oppositions are neutralised in weak syllables. ... The final syllables of polysyllabic Bribri morphemes are always strong syllables, as are those making up monosyllabic morphemes.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 110-111, sections 'Oposiciones tonales', 'Silabas fuertes y silabas debiles', 'Factores morfologicos'

(2) Deciding source is a 2017 703-pp instrumental phonology dissertation — the most thorough description of Bribri prosody that exists per Glottolog and per Chevrier's own literature survey (all earlier phonological work is 8-19-pp sketches or pedagogical). The 'morphological' coding (accent = morpheme-final, demarcative, prefixes excepted, one primary per word with morpheme-final secondaries) is exactly what both sources state. tone.says: Dedicated article on the interaction of nasality, tone and intensity. Two tone levels (high, low) which also combine on one vowel as high-low and low-high, established by minimal pairs; a strong vs weak syllable opposition (strong = more intense and longer; weak = open, only three of the seven vowels); tonal (and nasal) oppositions neutralised in weak syllables, low tone being the neutralisation value; morpheme-final syllables (and monosyllabic morphemes) are always strong, up to two weak sylla…

sources.note: Record + abstract (Dissertation Abstracts International 42-12A, via Penn catalog): comparative reconstruction from Guatuso, Cabecar, Bribri, Terraba, Boruca (author's field data) and Muisca; 'Descriptions of the phonemic systems of the six languages.. are included' (so a Bribri phonemic description with suprasegmentals is inside); Proto-Chibchan reconstructed with distinctive nasalization, stress, and two tones (high, low). The Bribri chapter itself was not seen; later authors (Coto-Solano 2015) cite it for Bribri's tone inventory.

sources.note: Excerpt as quoted by Constenla 1982 n.1 (German): 'Die Tonstufen sind im Bribri ziemlich wichtig und meines Wissens bisher unbeachtet geblieben. Die Sprache unterscheidet einem steigenden Ton, fallenden und eingehenden Ton, einen Hochton und Tiefton.. Beide finden sich gewoehnlich im Auslaut und dienen nicht selten zur Unterscheidung des Sinnes sonst scheinbar gleicher Woerter' - rising, falling, 'entering', high and low tones, mostly word-final, lexically distinctive; also distinguishes full vowels from reduced 'Gleitvokale' (weak syllables).
